scenes.say: What does s t d move actually do? Surprisingly little. It doesn't move anything. Let's read it.

scenes.head: The whole implementation (simplified)
scenes.say: This is essentially the whole function. Its body is one line: a static cast to an rvalue reference. The remove reference part just makes sure the result is a plain T and and, even when T was deduced as a reference. No memory is touched. No code runs at run time. It only changes how the compiler sees the expression: from something you're still using, to something that may be stolen from.

scenes.head: Proof: the cast alone does nothing
scenes.say: Proof. Cast a with s t d move and bind it to a reference. Nothing happened. a still prints hello. The steal happens only when that rvalue reaches something that takes an rvalue, here the string's move constructor. With G C C, a is now empty, size zero, but that's not guaranteed: it's valid but unspecified.

scenes.head: So the move constructor does the moving
scenes.say: So the chain is: first the cast. The expression becomes string and and, an x value, a kind of rvalue. Overload resolution now picks the move constructor over the copy constructor. And the move constructor steals the buffer. s t d move just enables that choice.

scenes.head: Three traps
scenes.say: Three traps. Writing return s t d move of a local stops the compiler from constructing it in place, and G C C with dash W all flags it as a pessimizing move. Just return s. Using s t d move on a const object gives a const rvalue, which can't bind to the move constructor, so it silently copies. And after a move, don't rely on the object's value. Assign it a new one, or let it be destroyed.

lines: std::move is just a cast to an rvalue reference. No code runs.
The move constructor or move assignment does the actual moving.
Don't move const objects, and don't return std::move(local).
scenes.say: s t d move is just a static cast to an rvalue reference. Nothing runs. The move constructor or move assignment does the actual work. Don't move const objects, and don't write return s t d move of a local.
